title: Pager Digest + Handoff: SRE sprint check (week of 2026-04-13)
content:
Purpose: quick weekly digest for SREs — incidents, SLO health, on-call handoff notes, and prioritized action items. Intended audience: SRE on-call, site reliability leads, platform engineers.

Summary at a glance:
- Incidents: 2 pager events this week (one elevated to P1 briefly, one P2). Both stabilized; P1 has a follow-up RCA scheduled.
- SLO status (MTD): availability 99.92% (target 99.95%), generation p95 latency MTD 380ms (target 350ms). Burn rate for availability is elevated; tracking in JIRA-RW-2381.
- On-call handoff: incoming rotation (week of 2026-04-20) assigned to Marco Chen. Handoff notes and outstanding tasks below.

Incident summaries:
1) Incident ID: INC-2026-041 (P1 -> mitigated to P2 within 40m)
   - Symptom: Increased 500s and timeouts for hosted-generation endpoints in us-west-2 between 03:12–03:48 UTC on 2026-04-15. Customer-visible latency and failed streams.
   - Timeline (high level):
     * 03:12 UTC — automated alerts: error rate spike + SLO alert fired.
     * 03:18 UTC — on-call paged (PagerDuty). Initial triage: surge in worker restarts across a subset of pods.
     * 03:25 UTC — mitigation: scale-up of dedicated pool and temporary routing to us-east-1 for high-priority traffic.
     * 03:40 UTC — error rate fell but some degraded responses persisted; degraded->resolved by 03:48 UTC.
   - Root cause (initial hypothesis): regression in the worker lifecycle handler that caused delayed draining during a rolling config rollout; resulted in unexpectedly high transient memory pressure + OOM kills on a shard.
   - Immediate mitigations performed: roll back rolling config change (was a new kernel selection flag), bumped pool size, enabled conservative draining.
   - Current status: systems stable, monitoring in normal range. Postmortem scheduled 2026-04-20 15:00 UTC (owners: Aisha, Sofia). Ticket: JIRA-RW-2381.
   - Open follow-ups: add a pre-rollout canary test for lifecycle changes (JIRA-RW-2390), update runbook step for rolling-update rollback.

2) Incident ID: INC-2026-042 (P2, short-lived cache warmup spike)
   - Symptom: brief spike in tokenization and KV-cache miss latency for several model variants at 09:05 UTC on 2026-04-14; caused p95 generation latency blips for ~11 minutes.
   - Root cause: cache eviction threshold miscalculation when model variants were updated; a batch of models missed the warm cache window.
   - Mitigation: manual cache preload for affected variants, adjusted eviction threshold to be more forgiving for cold-start windows.
   - Status: closed. Queue to add automated cache-prime step to deployment pipeline (JIRA-RW-2402).

SLO & monitoring snapshot:
- Availability SLO (monthly): target 99.95%
  * MTD: 99.92% — burn is visible; minor but actionable.
  * Next steps: accelerate JIRA-RW-2381 remediation items and consider temporary stricter routing to reserved capacity for critical routes.
- Generation latency SLO (p95, 512 tokens): target 350ms
  * MTD: 380ms. Contributors: higher tail during peak (14:00–16:00 UTC) due to batching thresholds hitting suboptimal windows.
  * Action: Sasha to test new batching heuristic in staging (JIRA-RW-2399).
- Error budget: remaining 0.7% for month; if no further incidents, still at risk. Recommend conservative rollout policy for next two weeks.

On-call handoff notes (outgoing: Aisha Patel; incoming: Marco Chen):
- Outstanding alerts to watch:
  * svc-gen-us-west-2: recent OOM pattern — watch host memory usage and pod restart counter.
  * cache-priming: job failures occasionally show 502 due to timeout; see JIRA-RW-2402.
- Active runbooks referenced during the week: runbooks/slo-monitoring, runbooks/rolling-update-rollback. Ensure both links in Confluence are up-to-date.
- Pager rotation: Marco takes primary on-call for 2026-04-20 -> 2026-04-27. Backup: Sofia.
- Escalation matrix reminder: if P1 persists >30m without clear mitigation, escalate to SRE lead + Eng infra (use escalation policy in Slack #sre-escalations).

Meeting notes: SRE weekly sync (2026-04-16 11:00 UTC)
- Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Sofia, Daniel, Sasha (guest)
- Topics covered: incident walk-through, SLO trend analysis, rehearsal for upcoming DR drill, and sprint planning for reliability tasks.
- Decisions made:
  * Prioritize the pre-rollout canary tests for lifecycle changes (owner: Sofia, JIRA-RW-2390).
  * Defer noncritical telemetry retention expansion to next sprint; critical dashboards only for now.
  * Run a dry-run of the DR failover to eu-west-1 on 2026-04-27 (owner: Daniel).

Action items (prioritized):
1) JIRA-RW-2381 — Full RCA and remediation plan for INC-2026-041 (owners: Aisha, Sofia). Deadline: 2026-04-23.
2) JIRA-RW-2390 — Implement pre-rollout canary test harness and add to CI gating (owner: Sofia). Deadline: 2026-05-07.
3) JIRA-RW-2399 — Evaluate new batching heuristic in staging, measure p95 improvements (owner: Sasha). Deadline: 2026-04-30.
4) JIRA-RW-2402 — Add automated cache-prime step to deploy pipeline and add observability for prime job (owner: Daniel). Deadline: 2026-04-28.
5) Update runbook: rolling-update-rollback — include explicit mem-pressure checks and emergency rollback commands (owner: Marco). Deadline: 2026-04-22.

Notes to the incoming on-call (Marco):
- Quick wins: watch for the memory churn pattern — a simple emergency scale-up (2x) + route to alternate region buys us breathing room.
- If you see repeated OOM kills correlated with a config rollout, stop the rollout and trigger the rollback runbook; do not attempt partial fixes.
- Keep an eye on SLO dashboards: availability and generation p95. If multiple alerts cluster, treat as systemic not isolated.

Unresolved questions / risks:
- How aggressively do we need to throttle self-serve hosted traffic vs reserved capacity when error budget is low? Conversation needed with product-hosted-api (ticketed follow-up).
- Do current CI canaries catch lifecycle handler regressions? Early signs say no — need more realistic failure injection in canaries.

Appendix / quick references:
- Short links: runbooks/slo-monitoring, runbooks/rolling-update-rollback, confluence:incidents/INC-2026-041 (will be created after RCA).
- Next sync: 2026-04-23 11:00 UTC — focus: RCA review, batching A/B test plan, DR runbook rehearsal.

End of digest. Ping me on Slack if anything needs immediate re-prioritization.
